Appearances:
Ms. Megha Sharma and Sh. Ritesh Saxena, Advocates for the appellants.
Sh. Kundan Lal, Chief PP for the State/Respondent No.1 Respondent nos. 2, 3 and 4 are Proforma respondents.

JUDGMENT:
1. This judgment shall decide the present appeal preferred by the appellants under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing order dated 18.11.2021 passed by Sh. D. Karthikeyan, Adjudicating Officer/Addl.

whereby, the appellant have been imposed consolidated penalty of Rs.
One Lakh for violation of Section 26 (2) (ii) and 27 (1) read with Section 3 (1) (i) of the FSS Act,
punishable under Section 54 of the FSS Act.

BRIEF FACTS:
2.
In a nutshell, the proforma respondent No. 4 M/

s. J.V. Restaurant Private Limited is a Company and engaged in the business of running Restaurants in Delhi, under the name & style 'The Town House Cafe' having its registered office at N63/64, Munshi Lal Building, Outer Circle, Connaught Place, New Delhi and the respondent No.2 Sh. Vineet Dhingra was the FBOcumChef in the said Cafe whereas the appellants are the Directors of the respondent No.4.

It is stated that on 09.03.2018 at about 2.46 p.m. Sh. Bal Mukund, the Food Safety Officer alongwith other officials visited the premises for inspection, which was fully co operated by the the respondent Nos. 2 and four portions of 'Prepared Dal Tadka' were bought for analysis, for which credit note of Rs. 1,502/ dated 09.03.2018 was given.

It is stated that on 01.10.2018 a complaint was filed by the FSO against the appellants and the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 under the Rule 3.1.1.(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 in the Court of Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate concerned and a reply was filed by the appellants on 21.01.2019, who considered the Food Analyst report No.
FSS/231/2018 dated 22.03.2018 and formed an opinion that the the samples were containing extraneous matter viz. vegetable oil in contravention of Section 26 (2) (ii), which led to the passing of the impugned order dated 18.11.2021.

GROUNDS OF APPEAL:
3.

The impugned order is assailed inter alia on the grounds that the Adjudicating Officer failed to correctly interpret Section 3 (1) (i) of FSS Act that would indicate that 'vegetable oil' does not come Rajesh Subramaniam vs Food Safety Officer on 27 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120781832/
2 under the definition of 'extraneous matter' as it is not carried from the raw materials or any packaging materials or process system used for its manufacture; and that the Food Safety Officer as well as Field Assistants had not followed the guidelines for sample collection in terms of Clause 1 of subRule 2.4.1 of Rule 2.4 of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011; and that the impugned order was passed without issuing any summons to the Chef i.e., respondent No.2; and that the Adjudicating Officer failed to appreciate that there was no question of commission of any cheating since edible vegetable oil is normally used to cook food and no food could be cooked in butter only,
particularly when FSS Act no where prescribes recipe of 'Dal Tadka', that is required to be followed;
and that the Adjudicating Officer failed to appreciate that proforma respondent No.4 viz. M/s. J.V.
Restaurant Private Limited has gone into liquidation and Resolution Professional has been appointed subsequent to the winding up order and there is applicable moratorium by virtue of section 14 of the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code.

sentences.text: 4. On filing of the appeal, notice was ordered to be issued to the respondent and although no reply has been filed, the present appeal is vehemently opposed.

DECISION:
5. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the Ld. Counsel for the rival parties at the Bar.
I have gone through the record of the Adjudicating Officer and record of the present appeal and documents filed therewith.

6. In order to decide the present appeal, it would be expedient to refer to relevant provisions under FSS Act and in this regard Section 3 (1) (i) of the Act provides as under: " 3 (1) (i) "extraneous matter" means any matter contained in an article of food which may be carried from the raw materials, packaging materials or process systems used for its manufacture or which is added to it,
but such matter does not render such article of food unsafe"

7. Further, section 26 of the FSS Act provides for the responsibility of the Food Business Operators and subSection (1) provides that every Food Business Operator shall ensure that articles of food satisfy requirement of the Act as also Rules and Regulations framed thereunder for each stages of production, processing, import,
distribution and sale; and subSection (2) (ii) provides that no Food Business Operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell, or distribution any article of food which is misbranded or sub standard or contains extraneous matter.
The whole crux of the Section 26 (2) of the Act is that no food which is unsafe should be manufactured, stored or to be sold.

Further, Section 27 imposes liability of manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers in case requirement of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder are not followed and subSection 3 under this Act creates liability for keeping any article of food in unhygienic condition, misbranded or else unsafe or sold after the date of expiry.

8. Reverting back to the instant appeal, it is admitted fact that four samples of 'Dal Tadka' were taken for analysis and as per report in the prescribed Form 'B' by the Rajesh Subramaniam vs Food Safety Officer on 27 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120781832/
3

sentences.text:
Food Analyst, an opinion was given to the effect that "sample contains extraneous matter viz. added vegetable oil in contravention of Section 26 (2) (ii) read with the definition of extraneous matter as defined under Section 3 (1) (i) of the Food Safety &
Standards Act, 2006'.

Assuming for the sake of convenience that the samples were lifted as per the prescribed procedure, interestingly, proforma report vide Column No. (8) provides that "DGHS Manual was followed for method as testing and no discrepancy was found with regard to prescribed standards for food safety by writing remarks (negative).

Further, the learned Adjudicating Officer in the impugned order found no basis in the complaint that 'vegetable oil' used in preparation of 'Dal Tadka' was coming within the purview of 'extraneous matter',.

However, in the same vain it was held that by virtue of definition in Section 3 (1) (i) of the FSS Act, the food was not "unsafe for human consumption"
9.

All said and done, it appears that the Adjudicating Officer was swayed that no plausible reason had been given by the appellants for not disclosing usage of 'vegetable oil' in preparation of 'Dal Tadka' at the time of lifting of the sample and it was held to be an act of cheating.

I am afraid, the Adjudicating Officer has failed to appreciate that edible vegetable oils are generally used for preparation of food articles in the nature of 'Dal Tadka' and as was rightly canvassed by the learned Counsel for the appellants, butter is also mixed to give it an added with other spices so as to create a distinct kind of flavour and taste to the recipe.

The case foisted by the Food Safety Officer is not one of 'misbranding' within the meaning of Section 3 (1) (zf)
since 'Dal Tadka' by very nature is a special dietary recipe.

Incidentally, Section 48(2)
of the FSS Act provides that in determining whether any food is unsafe or injurious to health, regard shall be had to the normal conditions of use of the food by the consumer vide subclause (a) (i) and its handling at each stage of production,
processing and distribution.

In other words, use of edible vegetable oil for preparation of 'Dal Tadka' is an essential ingredient of cooking and can not be said to be an extraneous matter having regard to the ordinary process of cooking of such recipe and its normal condition of use by the consumers.

Hence, it is a case where by virtue of Section 80 (B) (2) (e) of the FSS Act, the appellants are able to show that they had no reason to suspect at the time of commission of the alleged offence that mere omission to mention use of 'edible vegetable oil' in preparation of 'Dal Tadka'
would constitute cheating upon the consumers and thus an offence under the Act.
10. In view of the foregoing discussion, the present appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 18.11.2021, whereby penalty has been imposed under Section 54 of the FSS Act, is hereby quashed.
11. The record of the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate alongwith copy of this Judgment be sent back.
File of appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
